finding.claim: Blind SSRF: the user-supplied callbackUrl is stored with no validation and later POSTed to by a periodic job. An attacker can register internal targets (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/, http://localhost:port/admin, internal service hosts) and make the server send POST requests with the payload to them every minute. The response is discarded, so the SSRF is blind, but it can still reach internal services and metadata endpoints.

trace.note: subscribe(name, callbackUrl) receives the attacker-controlled URL
stored in the subscriptions map unvalidated (no scheme, host, or IP check)
notifyAll iterates the stored values every minute
URI.create(cb) builds the request URI with no allowlist
client.send issues the POST to the attacker-chosen URL

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host or IP allowlist or denylist exists in subscribe or notifyAll. No auth check is visible in this file (the route handler is not present). HttpClient.newHttpClient() has default redirect policy NEVER, which does not limit the destination. The only check is none; the response body is ignored, so the SSRF is blind.

verdict.reason: src/Jobs.java:14 stores callbackUrl unvalidated and :21-24 POSTs to it via URI.create/client.send, with no host or scheme check anywhere (the only regex guard at :30 is in the unrelated thumb()); the 1-minute schedule is only a comment at :17 and the route and auth code are not in the repo, so the "every minute" claim and attacker reachability rest on the comments.
